key_insight: Transformer plasticity and stability depend differently on module function: QK/VO projections learn procedures most readily, while MLPs excel at declarative memorization.
engineering_relevance: Module-targeted updates could help engineering AI systems acquire new procedures while preserving stored knowledge, though solid-mechanics applications were not evaluated.
method: Separate procedural learning from declarative memorization in controlled synthetic tasks.
Compare plasticity and stability across QK, VO, and MLP modules.
Use targeted module reset-and-recovery experiments to probe functional dependencies.
evidence_signal: During new-procedure learning, QK updates retain over half of stored declarative memory, MLP updates retain far less, and VO updates lose roughly four-fifths; realistic-model experiments broadly echo these asymmetries.
watch_item: The abstract provides no solid-mechanics validation, so transfer to constitutive modeling remains unproven.
paper_title: Stability Does Not Mirror Plasticity: A Module-Level View of Declarative and Procedural Learning in Transformers
